name: When should I consider roof replacement instead of repair?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider roof replacement instead of repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider roof replacement if your roof is nearing the end of its expected lifespan (typically 20-25 years for asphalt shingles), if it has widespread damage across multiple sections, or if repairs are consistently needed. If the cost of repairs exceeds 25-30% of the cost of a new roof, replacement often provides better long-term value and peace of mind. A full assessment can help determine the most cost-effective and durable solution for your home.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider replacement if your roof is old, has widespread damage, or if repair costs approach 25-30% of a new roof.
